session_note: Texas has no regular session in even years; the 89th Legislature's only regular session (89R) ran 2025-01-14 through sine die 2025-06-02, so any 89R bill not enrolled and signed by sine die is dead with no carryover into 2026. The Governor called at least two special sessions of the 89th Legislature later in 2025 (session codes visible in the capitol.texas.gov session directory), whose agendas were dominated by redistricting and disaster/flood relief; no evidence was found on capitol.texas.gov that any of the data-center/large-load/tax-exemption bills below were placed on a special-session call or refiled under an 89S bill number.

decisions.notes: SJR 72 is a proposed constitutional amendment (enabling legislation for SB 2222/HB 5588's ad valorem exemption). As a joint resolution it would be 'enacted' by voter ratification at an election, not by gubernatorial signature, if the legislature had adopted it by the required two-thirds vote and placed it on the ballot. It never reached a floor vote in either chamber, so bill_status_category is failed_died rather than passed_both_chambers or enacted; it was never submitted to voters.
